episode_title: Ep 27. Succession by Design, Not Default – Jeff Schrock, VAA – CEO 2 CEO

real_qa.q: Why is VAA planning a CEO succession and what timeline did Jeff Schrock announce to the board?
real_qa.r: Jeff Schrock announced in November 2023 to his board that he intends to transition from CEO either at the end of 2026 or the end of 2027, giving approximately three years' notice. His decision was driven by recognizing that after almost 10 years as CEO, he questioned the highest and best use of his time, felt exhaustion from leading through the pandemic, and realized the company's $90 million BHAG target required capabilities he hadn't yet developed.
real_qa.requete: VAA CEO succession Jeff Schrock timeline 2026 2027

real_qa.q: How did VAA evaluate internal versus external CEO candidates and what was the final decision?
real_qa.r: VAA spent all of 2024 modeling internal versus external CEO options in parallel. The company identified an internal candidate named Brian and evaluated 15 key attributes needed in a leader, including the ability to grow the company to $90 million. They ultimately decided that having Brian become CEO made the most sense, a decision finalized in late 2024 to early 2025.
real_qa.requete: VAA internal external CEO search decision Brian

real_qa.q: What gap in experience did VAA identify for its incoming CEO Brian, and how is the company addressing it?
real_qa.r: VAA recognized that Brian, like Jeff Schrock, had not run a $90 million company before. To address this gap, the company decided to add an outside board member starting in January who has actually led a $90 million company as CEO or COO, with that person serving as a close mentor to Brian on key elements of scaling to that size.
real_qa.requete: VAA new board member $90 million company CEO mentor

real_qa.q: Will Jeff Schrock remain at VAA after stepping down as CEO, and what role will he have?
real_qa.r: Yes, Jeff Schrock plans to stay at VAA through at least 2030-2032 and will remain as board chair. He will craft a new role focused on business development, client development, and helping staff grow—areas he enjoys. This continues a precedent at VAA: founder Dick Van Sickle stepped down as CEO in 2004 but stayed until 2009, and Scott Stanglin stepped down at end of 2013 but left in 2017.
real_qa.requete: Jeff Schrock staying VAA after CEO transition board chair

real_qa.q: How will Jeff Schrock ensure Brian's success as the new CEO and avoid the common pitfall of appearing to look over his shoulder?
real_qa.r: Schrock plans to be intentional about staying in his lane and directing questions to Brian rather than answering them himself. Success will be measured by clients and employees gravitating directly toward Brian for decisions, not looking to Schrock first. Though Schrock will remain active in the transition process, he emphasizes that Brian's freedom and perception as the true leader depends largely on Schrock intentionally staying out of the way.
real_qa.requete: CEO succession avoiding looking over shoulder new leader authority

He holds civil engineering licenses in 29 states and has been CEO for 13 active years, taking over in January 2014 when the company had approximately $14 million in revenue. He has led the firm's growth to $54 million in current revenue with a 10-year BHAG target of $90 million by 2030, and is intentional about building trust within teams through mentorship programs and employee development initiatives.
